title: Integrated Multi-Omics and Spatial Transcriptomics Reveal GUK1 as a Prognostic Biomarker Regulated by the TP53-HSF1 Axis in Breast Cancer.
authors: Lee, Wei; Lin, Hung-Yu; Chu, Pei-Yi
one_liner_zh: 该研究整合多组学与空间转录组学探究GUK1在乳腺癌中的预后作用及TP53-HSF1调控轴，虽含分子对接但核心为临床生物标志物与实验验证，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制研究。
abstract: Background: Guanylate kinase 1 (GUK1) is crucial for nucleotide metabolism, yet its impact on breast cancer (BC) progression remains poorly defined. The objective of the present study is to investigate GUK1 as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target. Methods: We employed a multi-omics approach integrating The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) data, machine learning algorithm, High-Definition spatial transcriptomics (Visium HD), single-cell profiling, molecular docking and experimental validation including in vitro knockdown models and Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR). Results: LASSO regression identified GUK1 as a key metabolic driver. High expression correlated significantly with poor survival and was most pronounced in Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2 (HER2)-positive and triple-negative subtypes. Spatial transcriptomics revealed GUK1 strongly colocalizes with expanding cancer cell nests, intensifying with disease stage. Single-cell analysis linked GUK1 overexpression to an immunosuppressive microenvironment enriched in exhausted T-cells. Clinically and molecularly, TP53 mutations are highly associated with HSF1 promoter hypomethylation and subsequent HSF1-mediated GUK1 upregulation. We experimentally confirmed this axis, showing that HSF1 or GUK1 knockdown significantly impaired cell migration and suppressed mTOR signaling. Furthermore, while high GUK1 levels predicted resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors, they enhanced sensitivity to the PI3K/mTOR inhibitor Apitolisib. This therapeutic vulnerability was validated by SPR, which confirmed high-affinity binding between GUK1 and Apitolisib, and by cell viability assays where GUK1 depletion induced drug resistance. Conclusion: GUK1 serves as a robust prognostic biomarker regulated by the TP53-HSF1 axis. Its distinct spatial patterns, immune-suppressive associations, and experimentally validated role in modulating PI3K/mTOR inhibitor sensitivity position GUK1 as a promising target for precision oncology in invasive BC.
abstract_zh: 背景：鸟苷酸激酶1（GUK1）对核苷酸代谢至关重要，但其在乳腺癌（BC）进展中的作用仍不明确。本研究旨在探讨GUK1作为预后生物标志物和治疗靶点的潜力。方法：我们采用多组学方法，整合癌症基因组图谱（TCGA）数据、机器学习算法、高清晰度空间转录组学（Visium HD）、单细胞分析、分子对接及实验验证，包括体外敲低模型和表面等离子体共振（SPR）。结果：LASSO回归将GUK1识别为关键代谢驱动因子。其高表达与较差生存率显著相关，且在人类表皮生长因子受体2（HER2）阳性和三阴性亚型中最为显著。空间转录组学显示，GUK1与扩张的癌细胞巢强烈共定位，并随疾病分期进展而增强。单细胞分析将GUK1过表达与富含耗竭T细胞的免疫抑制微环境相关联。在临床和分子层面，TP53突变与HSF1启动子低甲基化及随后的HSF1介导的GUK1上调高度相关。我们通过实验证实了这一轴，显示HSF1或GUK1敲低显著损害细胞迁移并抑制mTOR信号通路。此外，高GUK1水平预测对CDK4/6抑制剂耐药，但增强了对PI3K/mTOR抑制剂Apitolisib的敏感性。这一治疗脆弱性通过SPR得到验证，确认了GUK1与Apitolisib之间的高亲和力结合，并通过细胞活力实验证实，GUK1缺失诱导药物耐药性。结论：GUK1作为受TP53-HSF1轴调控的稳健预后生物标志物。其独特的空间模式、免疫抑制关联及在调节PI3K/mTOR抑制剂敏感性中的实验验证作用，使GUK1成为浸润性乳腺癌精准肿瘤学中一个有前景的靶点。
